observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 15 that half of Russia's six top diesel-producing refineries had significantly reduced or halted output in September after Ukrainian drone strikes.

Reuters separately reported that Russia and Ukraine continued energy-infrastructure strikes despite a U.S.-announced proposal for an energy truce: Russia launched about 200 drones overnight and hit Ukrainian energy/port infrastructure, while Ukraine struck the Syzran refinery and other facilities.

Reuters analysis said the global diesel market remains structurally tight because Russian and Gulf refinery/export disruptions have reduced available supply; any truce proposal remains unverified in implementation.
semantic_interpretation: The refined-product shock is no longer only a Middle East crude/shipping problem. Persistent damage and reduced runs at major Russian diesel refineries add a second independent supply constraint, increasing the probability that diesel, freight and industrial logistics costs remain elevated even if crude stabilizes. The proposed energy truce is not treated as effective until observable compliance exists.
